# TEM-t (Transformer with Recurrent Position Encodings)

**A transformer whose position encodings are generated by an action-driven RNN rather than fixed sines and cosines; it learns grid and band cells in those encodings, place cells in its memory neurons, and is shown *algebraically* to be [[wiki/entities/tolman-eichenbaum-machine.md]] with the softmax put back in.**

> **Provenance.** Whittington, Warren & Behrens 2022, *Relating Transformers to Models and Neural Representations of the Hippocampal Formation*, ICLR 2022 (`raw/whittington-2022-transformers-hippocampal-formation.md`). Same first author as TEM; the claim is a mathematical relationship between two architectures, not a representational resemblance — the authors say so explicitly, twice.

---

## The three modifications to a vanilla transformer

| # | Change | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Queries and keys read *only* the position encoding; values read *only* the stimulus.** `Q, K = ẼW_e`, `V = X̃ = XW_x` | The extreme of the empirical finding that transformers do best when position informs keys/queries but not values. It also *is* the `g`/`x` factorisation: retrieval is addressed structurally, content is what gets returned |
| 2 | **Causal mask** — keys and values hold `e_<t`, `x_<t`; the query is the present `e_t` | Not a language convention here: the agent has not yet experienced the future stimulus-position pairs, so masking is the memory store growing as it walks |
| 3 | **Position encodings generated recurrently**: `e_{t+1} = σ(e_t W_a)`, `W_a` learnable and **action-dependent** | Position encodings become learned, sequence-specific, and inferred on the fly instead of being a fixed table over integer offsets |

Trained on the TEM task family: predict the next sensory observation while walking graphs that share a structure (4-connected 2D, and a 6-connected hexagonal world) but randomly re-assign one-hot stimuli to nodes. Zero-shot accuracy — prediction across an edge never traversed, to a node already visited — is the metric that only generalised structural knowledge can move.

---

## The equivalence, in four lines

TEM writes conjunctions `p_τ = flatten(x̃_τᵀ g̃_τ)` into a Hebbian matrix `M_t = Σ_τ p_τᵀ p_τ` and reads them with an attractor. One attractor step, linear, is

| Step | Expression | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Attractor update | `q_t M_t = Σ_τ (q_t · p_τ) p_τ` | Memories weighted by dot-product similarity to the query — transformer self-attention **without the softmax** (Ramsauer et al. 2020's Hopfield↔transformer result) |
| Query by path integration, `q_t = flatten(1ᵀ g_t)` | `q_t · p_τ = (g̃_t · g̃_τ) · x̄̃_τ` | The outer-product memory makes the similarity factorise: attending with `g̃` alone scores memories by *structural* match only |
| Retrieved conjunction | `p_t^ret = (g̃_t G̃ᵀ) Λ_x P` | `Λ_x` diagonal, entries `x̄̃_τ = Σ_i (x̃_τ)_i` |
| Deconjunctified sensory component | `x̃_t^ret = (g̃_t G̃ᵀ) Λ_x Λ_g X̃ ≈ α · (g̃_t G̃ᵀ) X̃` | Compare `softmax(q_t Kᵀ/√d_k) V`. The `Λ` weightings must learn to be constant `α`, else some memories are preferentially retrieved regardless of query |

| TEM component | Transformer component |
|---|---|
| Path-integrated `g` (entorhinal) | Position encoding `e` |
| Sensory code `x` (lateral entorhinal) | Values `V` |
| Hebbian memory matrix `M` | The key/value cache |
| One attractor iteration | One self-attention block (stack them to iterate) |
| Writing `p_t` into `M` | Appending a token to the cache |
| `Λ_x, Λ_g` learned to be constant | The softmax normalisation |

**The load-bearing consequence.** The wiki's cleanest `p = f(g, x)` architecture and the dominant machine-learning architecture are the *same computation* with different normalisation, and neither was derived from the other. Whatever generality transformers have is therefore available to a hippocampal model, and whatever structural-transfer story TEM has is available to a transformer — which is the point the paper makes about language: nothing about the equivalence is spatial.

---

## Results

| Result | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Grid and band cells in the position encodings** | Rate maps and autocorrelations of the recurrent `e` units resemble recorded grid cells, with either linear or ReLU activation after the transition; band cells also appear; grids also form in a 6-connected hexagonal world. Reported with grid scores over the whole population (grid score > 0.3–0.5 conventionally counts) |
| **Place cells in the memory neurons** | Under Krotov & Hopfield 2020's neurally plausible split of attention into *feature* neurons (carrying the query) and *memory* neurons (computing `softmax(q_t Kᵀ)`), the memory neurons are sparsely active by construction and therefore have single-environment spatial fields. Scored by a novel metric: firing mass in the largest connected component of the rate map ÷ firing mass in all components — 1 for a clean single field. The metric cleanly separates RNN units (grid-like) from memory units (place-like) |
| **Those place cells remap randomly** | Neighbouring in one environment does not predict neighbouring in another, unlike grid cells, whose phase relationships are preserved |
| **Sample efficiency** | TEM-t reaches high zero-shot accuracy in far fewer samples than TEM, and in less wall-clock per gradient step; TEM-t was stopped at 20,000 updates against TEM's stated 50,000 |
| **Capacity** | TEM-t is stated to handle much larger problems with more stored memories — asserted, not plotted |

**The performance comparison is explicitly not fair** (the authors say so): TEM's public code was used unoptimised. What survives the caveat is the direction, not the factor.

---

## What the equivalence buys architecturally

**Multi-region conjunction becomes additive instead of multiplicative.** TEM binds two cortical regions by an outer product, so a third region `c̃` multiplies the hippocampal cell count by `n_c`. In TEM-t a third region needs `n_c` extra *feature* neurons and **no extra memory neurons** — one memory neuron can index a pattern across three or more areas. Proposed update, with `⊙` elementwise:

`c̃_t ← softmax((g̃_t G̃ᵀ) ⊙ (x̃_t X̃ᵀ)) C̃`   (alternative, less derived: `softmax(g̃_t G̃ᵀ + x̃_t X̃ᵀ) C̃`)

Any subset of the bound regions can reinstate the rest. This is **hippocampal indexing theory** (Teyler & Rudy 2007) made into an equation: the hippocampus stores no content, only an index binding cortical patterns, and the price of another modality is linear ([[wiki/concepts/complementary-learning-systems.md]]).

**Position encodings should carry the task's structure, not the sequence's ordinal.** Sines and cosines encode a *line*. TEM-t's encodings encode whatever structure the transition statistics have. The paper's extrapolation: the analogue for language is **grammar** — position encodings inferred on the fly from a previously learned structural repertoire. **(brainstorm)** This is the sharpest concrete proposal the wiki has for exporting `g` out of navigation: it requires no new architecture, only that the position encoding be produced by a learned recurrent operator keyed to a *relation* (a parse decision, an argument slot) instead of a clock.

**Cortex may be running the same circuit without a hippocampus.** Transformer representations predict language-area responses, and patients with major hippocampal damage speak and comprehend normally — so if the computation is transformer-shaped, the memory neurons for such tasks are cortical and short-term, and the hippocampus is needed only when memories must last or must bind across distant areas. That reframes hippocampal dependence as a property of the *memory horizon and the span of binding*, not of the computation ([[wiki/empirical-tensions.md]] T28).

---

## Implementation details worth stealing

| Detail | Why |
|---|---|
| **Adaptive inverse temperature `β ∝ log(n_memories)`** | The softmax denominator grows with the number of stored memories, so attention values would otherwise shrink as the agent explores. Standard transformers never face this because the set size is fixed |
| **LayerNorm (plain z-score) on the position encodings before attention** | Standardises the retrieval scores so no memory is up-weighted by the norm of its address |
| **Write a memory only if that `g`-`x` conjunction is not already stored** (dot-product check) | Otherwise attention is biased toward frequently revisited locations. TEM's Hebbian rule does this implicitly by storing only the un-predicted residual: `M = Σ_τ (p_τ − p̂_τ)ᵀ (p_τ + p̂_τ)` |
| **Drift correction as a second attention head** | Recurrent position encodings accumulate noise with no manifold to fall back on (unlike a hand-built continuous attractor). Query the store with the *stimulus* to get "what position encoding did I have last time I saw this landmark": `g_t^ret = f_θ(softmax(x̃_t X̃ᵀ ⊙ g_t^PI G̃) G̃)` — key/query on `x`, value on `g`. Then `g_t = g_t^PI + f_θ(g_t^ret, g_t^PI)(g_t^ret − g_t^PI)`, a learned gate between integration and recall |
| **The combination is multiplicative, not additive** | Both here and in the multi-iteration update `x̃_t ← softmax(x̃_t X̃ᵀ ⊙ g̃_t G̃ᵀ) X̃` (first iteration `softmax(g̃_t G̃ᵀ) X̃`), the derived way to condition on two cues is an elementwise product of two attention score vectors — the paper flags this as counter-intuitive. It is an AND over two addressing channels, where a sum would be an OR |
| **Losses** | Two next-observation cross-entropies (one queried with `g^PI`, one with the inferred `g`), a squared error between `g` and `g^PI`, L2 on weights and on `g` |

---

## Limitations

| Limit | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **No capacity win** | Krotov & Hopfield's biologically plausible split needs **one memory neuron per memory**, so storage stays linear in neuron count. The `2^{N/2}` scaling proved for exponential-activation modern Hopfield networks (Demircigil et al. 2017) is *not* inherited. The speed-up is real; the capacity argument is not — and gap G42 is untouched |
| **Random remapping contradicts the data** | Memory-neuron place cells remap randomly, but place cells are measured to remap consistently with a preserved grid code ([[wiki/empirical-tensions.md]] T39/T40, from this author's own earlier work). The paper's repair: hippocampal *feature* neurons `g̃ = gW_g` inherit the grid relationship, so a population effect survives while individual memory neurons do not. Untested |
| **Softmax not ablated** | Whether place-like fields need the softmax, or appear for any activation that keeps memory neurons sparse, is conjectured and explicitly left to future work |
| **One block, one iteration** | Simulations use a single transformer block with a single attention iteration; multi-iteration retrieval is derived but not run |
| **Same task envelope as TEM** | Actions/relations are supplied and labelled (hardness source 2 untouched) and stimuli are i.i.d. across nodes by design, so sensory correlations — which are what real worlds offer and what a cheaper non-structural solution would exploit — are never tested |
| **The grid-cell result inherits the standard audit gap** | Grid scores are reported for the full population, which is better than most, but fraction-of-runs, seed sensitivity and module structure are not ([[wiki/concepts/objective-identifiability.md]]). What it *does* supply against T38: the target here is a one-hot categorical over stimulus identities, so no centre–surround readout kernel exists to install the periodicity |

**Hardness-source coverage** ([[wiki/concepts/latent-graph-discovery.md]]): source 1 ✓ · source 3 ✓ · source 4 ✓ · sources 2, 5, 6 ✗ — identical to TEM, as the equivalence requires.

## Connections

- **[[wiki/entities/tolman-eichenbaum-machine.md]]** — the same model with the softmax removed and the attractor iterated: this page's derivation converts TEM's Hebbian outer-product store into a key/value cache, its path-integrated `g` into a position encoding, and buys a large speed-up plus additive (rather than multiplicative) scaling in the number of bound cortical regions — at the cost of relocating place cells from conjunctive cells to memory neurons, which changes what remapping should look like.
- **[[wiki/concepts/attention.md]]** — the strongest form of that page's "attention weights are a soft adjacency" brainstorm: here self-attention *is* a Hebbian associative memory read, the keys are structural addresses and the values are content, so one attention head is exactly one integrate-then-retrieve step over a stored graph.
- **[[wiki/concepts/path-integration.md]]** — recasts position encodings as path integration and vice versa: `e_{t+1} = σ(e_t W_a)` is this page's update rule wearing a transformer's clothes, which makes an ordinal positional code the degenerate case (a single action repeated) of a structural one.
- **[[wiki/concepts/abstract-structural-codes.md]]** — supplies the export route for `g` out of navigation: a position encoding generated by a learned action-keyed operator can carry grammar or task structure as readily as space, and the same equations then apply unchanged.
- **[[wiki/concepts/pattern-separation-completion.md]]** — sparsity here is produced by the softmax over memory neurons rather than by a sparse expansion, so separation becomes a normalisation choice; and retrieval from either factor alone (`g` → what is here, `x` → where was I) is pattern completion of a conjunction from one of its parts.
- **[[wiki/concepts/complementary-learning-systems.md]]** — hippocampal indexing theory in closed form, with the scaling result that makes it worth having: one index neuron can bind three or more cortical areas, so the fast store's cost is linear in the number of modalities bound.
- **[[wiki/concepts/latent-graph-discovery.md]]** — the meta/instance split expressed in a transformer's own vocabulary: slow weights (`W_a`, the transition operators) hold the meta-graph, the key/value cache holds this environment's instance-graph, and the causal mask is the store growing as evidence is gathered.
- **[[wiki/entities/maze-solving-transformers.md]]** — the same architecture examined from the other end: there a generic decoder is probed and found to hold a graph it cannot reliably navigate, here a decoder is *constructed* so that its position encodings must path-integrate — which makes the graph a property of the update rule instead of something the objective may or may not induce.
- **[[wiki/concepts/neuroscience-ai-transfer.md]]** — an unusual case: no transfer occurred in either direction (transformers were built with no reference to the brain) and the relationship was found afterwards, which makes it evidence about convergence rather than about import.
- **[[wiki/concepts/working-memory.md]]** — the key/value cache is the addressable store, the query is the read, and the write policy is explicit (store only novel conjunctions) — one of the few places in the wiki where a memory architecture states when *not* to write.
